title: docs(adr): record ADR-0076 OQ#9 worklist item (4)'s outcome — env resolution is seam-first across the audited pair, with one consumer measured off it
body:
Fixes #9058

⚠️ **`docs/adr/**` — maintainer merges this by hand** (Prime Directive #14). Left as **draft**, not queued, no auto-merge.

## What this changes

One new bullet under ADR-0076 Open Question 9, recording the outcome of D11 worklist item **(4) — unify env-resolution on the injected `KernelResolver` seam**. Items (1)(2)(3) each had their outcome recorded under that entry; (4) was never mentioned again, so the ADR kept reading as an open obligation while the seam had been serving requests for months.

**No code changes.** The one defect the audit turned up is filed separately (see below) rather than ridden along — mixing a behaviour change into a maintainer-merged ADR PR is exactly what Prime Directive #14 makes expensive.

## The measurement came first, and it did not come out where the card guessed

The card (#9058) was explicit that it had measured only "the seam exists, and the dispatcher's env resolution goes through it", and ⛔ did **not** assert full discharge. So the first step was auditing every env-resolution call site — every site that answers *"which environment does this request belong to"* from request-borne signals — against `main` @ `ba2e3c172`. Result: **partial**, and the entry says partial.

| surface | on the seam? | measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime/http-dispatcher.ts` | yes | one decision per request; `packages/runtime/src` holds **zero** `env-registry` / `resolveByHostname` reads |
| `runtime/domain-handler-registry.ts` | yes | direct-caller kernel swap reads the same seam |
| `rest/rest-server.ts` | seam-first | one shared entry point, **8** consumers; host resolver consulted first, normal return final |
| `plugin-hono-server` current-user trio | yes | `kernel-resolver` per request, structural interface declared locally |
| `rest-server.ts` legacy chain | no (deliberate) | hostname → `X-Environment-Id` → default, retained beneath the seam for resolver-less hosts |
| `rest-server.ts` `probeMcpServeable` | **no (gap)** | the 9th consumer; re-derives its own environment — filed as #9120 |
| `cloud-connection-plugin.ts` | no | own closure, **8** handlers |
| `runtime-config-plugin.ts` | no | own hostname chain, two registry spellings |
| `cli/.../serve.ts` hostname guard | no | hostname *existence* only |

Two findings that differ from the card and are reported as measured, not smoothed over:

1. **Item (4) landed in two tranches under two different ADR attributions.** The card attributed the seam to ADR-0006 Phase 5 — true of the dispatcher tranche. But `rest-server.ts` and `rest-api-plugin.ts` cite **ADR-0076 D11 step ④** by name. A reader auditing only the dispatcher's citation would credit the whole item to ADR-0006 and never find the half naming this decision. The entry records both.
2. **"Unify" was delivered as seam-first with a documented fallback**, not as deletion of the parallel chain. The entry says so explicitly and marks ⛔ *do not read "unified" as "the hostname/header chain is gone"*.

## Shape follows the merged D11 revision (#9057)

Same three habits, applied where they have a subject: figures **re-derived** at `ba2e3c172` rather than copied from source comments; limits **named** rather than rounded away; the reading a later reader must not inherit marked ⛔. Where a habit has no subject it is not manufactured — no prior ADR wording is falsified by this audit, so nothing is marked `superseded`.

One thing the entry refuses on the record: **the tranches are not dated.** This clone is shallow (155 reachable commits), so `git log -S` bottoms out at the graft boundary and returns the same unrelated commit for every probe. Attribution is read from source citations; a landing date quoted here would be fabrication. Same measurement hazard the D11 revision already records for the retired line-count series.

## Out-of-scope finding

**#9120** — `RestServer.probeMcpServeable` re-derives the request's environment instead of using the shared entry point, so `/discovery`'s `mcp` advertisement can follow the host kernel rather than the request's environment on a hostname-routed multi-tenant host. Filed unassigned, unlabeled for triage; #9120 remains open and is not addressed by this PR. Its sibling `resolveRegisteredServices` — which the probe's own doc-comment claims parity with — *does* reach the entry point, which is what makes it a gap rather than a design choice.

## Verification

Gate union re-run **after** the final commit, at `git rev-parse --short HEAD` = **`3b3bf65fa`** (working tree clean at that sha). Families derived from the changed path with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs docs/adr/0076-objectql-core-tiering.md`, which named three; `check:nul-bytes` added because any edit implicates it.

```

node scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs

  121 decision number(s) ...; 25840 citation(s) across 3224 file(s) resolve).
```
